3: Deres tanker forekom ham frugtbare, mens han læste dem, eller når han ledte efter argumenter mod konkurrerende teorier, særligt de materialistiske; men så snart han vendte sig for at finde en løsning på problemerne for sig selv, skete det samme hver gang. Så længe han holdt fast i de fastlagte definitioner af dunkle ord som _ånd, vilje, frihed, væsen_, og bevidst lod sig falde i de ordfælder, filosofferne lagde for ham, syntes han at forstå noget. Men i samme øjeblik han trådte ud af den kunstige tankekæde og vendte sig fra selve livet tilbage til det, der havde tilfredsstillet ham, mens han tænkte efter de definitioners regler, faldt hele den kunstige struktur sammen som et korthus, og det blev klart, at strukturen var bygget op af de ombyttede ord, uden noget vigtigere end fornuften til at holde den sammen.

Tankerne forekom ham frugtbare, når han læste eller selv fandt på indvendinger mod andre læresystemer, især det materialistiske. Men så snart han læste eller selv udtænkte svar på spørgsmålene, gentog det samme sig altid. Når han fulgte en given definition af uklare ord som _ånd, vilje, frihed, substans_ og med vilje gik i den ordfælde, som filosofferne eller han selv havde stillet op, syntes han at begynde at forstå noget. Men så snart han forlod den kunstige tankegang og fra livet vendte tilbage til det, der havde tilfredsstillet ham, mens han fulgte den bestemte tanketråd, styrtede hele det kunstige bygningsværk sammen som et korthus. Det blev klart, at det var bygget af de samme ord, blot omstillet, uden forbindelse til noget i livet, der var vigtigere end fornuften.

3: Their ideas seemed fruitful to him when he was reading them, or when he was looking for arguments against rival theories, especially the materialist ones; but as soon as he turned to find a solution to the problems for himself, the same thing always happened. As long as he stuck to the fixed definitions of obscure words like _spirit, will, freedom, essence_, deliberately letting himself fall into the verbal traps the philosophers laid for him, he seemed to be understanding something. But the moment he stepped away from the artificial chain of reasoning and turned from life itself back to what had satisfied him while he was thinking by the rules of those definitions, the whole artificial structure fell apart at once like a house of cards, and it became clear that the structure had been built up out of those rearranged words, with nothing more important than reason to hold it together.

These ideas seemed fruitful when he read or devised objections to other doctrines, especially materialism. But as soon as he read or devised answers to the questions themselves, the same thing always happened. Following a given definition of obscure words such as _spirit, will, freedom, substance_, deliberately entering the verbal trap the philosophers or he himself had set, he seemed to begin to understand something. But once he left that artificial train of thought and returned from life to what had satisfied him while he followed that particular thread, the whole artificial structure suddenly collapsed like a house of cards. It was clear that it was built of the same words, merely rearranged, independently of something in life more important than reason.
